events.text: At its 2006 IPO, Constellation set an objective of generating average annual revenue growth per share and EBITDA growth per share in excess of 20% for the five-year period January 1, 2006 through December 31, 2010.
events.source_title: Constellation Software Inc. To Our Shareholders (compiled President's letters)

events.item: IPO growth target progress note (FY2007 letter)
events.text: After two years of the five-year objective, Constellation reported 16% net revenue growth and 33% EBITDA growth for 2007 (following 27% and 31% respectively in 2006), and stated it continued to believe the 20%-per-year, five-year objective would be 'challenging, but achievable.'

events.text: On April 4, 2011, Constellation's board announced a review of strategic alternatives to enhance shareholder value, retaining BofA Merrill Lynch and BMO Capital Markets as advisors, with no defined timeline and no assurance the review would lead to any transaction.
events.source_title: Constellation Software Inc. to Evaluate Strategic Alternatives

events.text: The strategic review did not result in a sale; Constellation remained independent. Per third-party accounts, the board adopted a quarterly dividend of $1.00 per share starting Q1 2012 (after paying $2 per share in total for 2011), and large institutional holders such as OMERS obtained liquidity by selling shares in the market (e.g., ~994,800 shares for about C$89.5 million in May 2012) rather than through a company sale.

gaps: WebFetch and curl are unavailable in this environment (per task rules); all figures came from WebSearch's own synthesized snippets of source pages/PDFs, not from directly reading the full documents, in both pass 1 and pass 2. Several figures should still be re-verified by a stage that can read the source PDFs/HTML directly (especially q4_2010_press_release.pdf and pr_q4_2012.pdf, which were each queried multiple times across both passes with broadly consistent results, increasing confidence but not eliminating this caveat).

FY2007 and FY2008 full-year revenue and net income in exact dollar terms remain UNRESOLVED after a second pass of 30 further targeted searches (including direct dollar-figure queries like '$243 million' / '$271 million' for 2007 and '$330 million' / '$333 million' for 2008). Only the third-party aggregator (eulerpool.com) figures exist. The company's own FY2007 and FY2008 results releases were repeatedly located by exact title/URL on csisoftware.com but WebSearch could not surface their dollar figures in either pass.

FY2009 full-year revenue is still a derived estimate (from the FY2010 release's stated 44% growth over 2009) rather than a directly sourced figure; no FY2009 press release itself was located with WebSearch in either pass. However, FY2009 Adjusted Net Income ($62 million), diluted EPS ($2.95), and cash flow from operations ($82 million) WERE newly found in pass 2, via the FY2010 release's comparative figures -- FY2009 net_income_attributable (a distinct GAAP metric) is still not found.

KNOWN DEFECT 2 (FY2011 net income attributable conflict, $157M vs $63M): pass 2 performed 3 additional targeted searches on this specific conflict. Two independent retrievals of pr_q4_2012.pdf both returned $157 million for FY2011 (paired consistently with $93 million for FY2012, and with a stated $75 million FY2011 tax recovery vs. an $18 million FY2012 tax expense). No retrieval reproduced $63 million or its paired $87 million FY2012 figure. This pass's assessment is that $157 million is the correct figure and $63 million is a likely retrieval/cross-year error (possibly confused with FY2009's $62 million Adjusted Net Income). Both entries are retained in figures per the intake spec's conflict rule; this is a reasoned resolution based on repeated independent retrieval, not a document-verified one, since the underlying PDF text still could not be read directly.

Could not confirm the exact year/release in which Constellation's dividend terminology changed from 'Declares Annual Dividend' (confirmed in FY2007 and FY2008 release titles) to a true quarterly cadence. Third-party sources suggest the real quarterly dividend (four payments/year) began Q1 2012, just after this window, with FY2010's and FY2011's dividends paid on more of an annual/lump basis; this was not confirmed from a primary FY2009 or FY2011 release title via WebSearch in either pass.

FY2009 press release (exact title, e.g. '...Year Ended December 31, 2009...') was never located via WebSearch despite multiple query variants across both passes; only the 2009 President's letter was found directly, plus FY2009 comparative figures embedded in the FY2010 release (which did yield several new FY2009 figures in pass 2 -- see figures above).

The following spec items remain UNFOUND for most or all years in the FY2007-FY2011 window even after pass 2: maintenance_recurring_revenue (annual totals, all years), net_income_attributable for FY2009, cash_from_operations for FY2007/FY2008/FY2010/FY2011, fcfa2s (this metric name postdates the window; 'adjusted net income' was the era's term, as recorded), acquisitions_cash_spent and acquisition_count for FY2007/FY2009/FY2010/FY2011 (FY2008 approximate figures were found in pass 2), shares_outstanding for all five years (pass 2 ran 1 additional dedicated search; only current/recent share-count aggregator pages were returned, no historical 2007-2011 figures), roic_plus_organic_pct for FY2008-FY2011, capex for all years, and total company employee headcount for all years (an FY2011 R&D-only headcount of ~1,022 was found in pass 2, which is NOT total employees).

roic_pct (company-stated, annual) was found only for FY2009 (24%, from the 2009 President's letter); no other year's ROIC was located as a clean annual figure. A third-party source (sbo.financial, 'Building an $88 billion M&A Machine') states Constellation's ROIC 'ran between 22 and 28 percent' across 2007-2009 broadly, but gives no year-by-year breakdown; this was NOT recorded as a per-year figures entry because doing so would require inventing a specific number from a stated range, which the intake spec prohibits.

Homeowner/Perseus and Emphasys operating groups: could not confirm whether or when they existed as named operating groups within the FY2007-2011 window, or their formation/acquisition dates, in either pass. Only Volaris, Harris, Jonas, and Friedman were positively confirmed as existing operating groups touching this era.

Could not confirm from the FY2010 results release or the 2010 President's letter text itself (only located by URL/title) whether Constellation explicitly stated that the 2006-2010, >20%-per-year IPO growth objective had been met; pass 2 ran an additional dedicated search on this exact question and again could not recover an explicit end-of-period verdict from search snippets. Only third-party secondary commentary claims it was exceeded.

Exact currency and full breakdown (regular vs special) of dividends declared for FY2007, FY2008, FY2009, and FY2011 were not confirmed in either pass; only a single FY2010-declared amount ($2.00/share, currency assumed CAD but unconfirmed) and a third-party claim of '$2 a share for 2011 in total' were found.

The 2011-2012 strategic review's conclusion date ('early 2012' per the task prompt) was not pinned to a specific month or a specific company press release in pass 2 despite 2 dedicated searches; third-party sources (two independent ones, both cited above) confirm only that the review concluded in '2012' with no sale, coinciding with the Q1 2012 adoption of a true quarterly dividend.

Number of acquisitions per year (a specific spec ask) was only approximately resolved for FY2008 (~17, from the 2008 letter's 'Maximus assets and 16 other businesses' wording) in pass 2. FY2007, FY2009, FY2010, and FY2011 acquisition counts remain unfound despite a dedicated pass-2 search across all five years; general context (e.g., '85 acquisitions over a 13 year period' as of a Q3 2008 letter) exists but does not isolate individual-year counts within the window.

No acquisition above USD 50 million (the task's event threshold) was identified anywhere in the FY2007-2011 window despite dedicated searching in both passes; the largest identified is the ~US$40 million Maximus assets deal (Sept 2008), which is recorded as an event for completeness but explicitly flagged as below threshold.

Search budget: pass 1 used 30 searches; this second pass used all 30 additional searches allotted to it, for a combined total of 60 searches across both passes, per the intake spec's 'use them all if gaps remain' instruction. Several of the remaining gaps above would likely only be resolved by a stage that can directly read the identified source PDFs (csisoftware.com q4_2007_shareholders_report.pdf, shareholder-letter---2009.pdf, shareholder-letter---2010.pdf, q4_2010_press_release.pdf, pr_q4_2012.pdf, csu-2011-aif.pdf, and the FY2007/FY2008 annual results releases by their confirmed URLs) rather than further WebSearch queries, since WebSearch's synthesized snippets have now been queried heavily on the same documents across two passes with diminishing new detail.
